Developing and releasing safedata

Source: build_notes.md

This repository and package uses a number of systems that you need to be aware of if you plan to work with the codebase:

  • The repository uses trunk based releases from the main branch with changes accepted into main only through pull requests. We used to use the git flow approach with release branches from develop onto main but moved to trunk based releases from version 2.0.0.
  • Documentation for the package is maintained using roxygen2 and pkgdown.
  • The code uses the pre-commit package to carry out QA checking on commits.
  • The repository uses GitHub Actions to carry out out checks on pull requests to support continuous integration.

These notes provide a brief walk through for these systems and some package specific requirements for releases.

Code development

Any new feature or bug fix should start with a new GitHub issue and then the creation of a new branch to implement the new code. Make a pull request from that branch onto main with code to add and document the new code: you will need to request a review and wait for code QA to pass before the PR can be merged. New releases are made directly from the main branch, following merged pull requests for features and bug fixes that are going to be included in the new release.

The repository includes a uvr.toml configuration file for the uvr package manager for R. It is highly recommended that you download and use uvr to manage the development environment for the package.

  • The uvr sync command will create and update a local R library (.uvr/library) containing all of the packages required to develop and run the code in the repository.
  • The uv run command can be used to run specific R script files.
  • Alternatively source .uvr/activate can be used to activate the configured R environment. While the environment is activated, all R commands will use the configured package setup.

If you do not use uvr, look at the uvr.toml file for the package and development requirements.

The package uses semantic version numbering and code on the development branch should use the prerelease token 9000. This is explained in more detail below in the description of the release cycle.

Package documentation

R packages require a man directory containing Rd format files that provide package documentation. Rather than maintain separate files manually, the roxygen2 package allows R objects to be documented directly in the R code files. The roxygen2 package can then be used to automatically rebuild and organise the man directory when documentation in the R source files changes.

The devtools package provides a wrapper function that can be run to updates man files:

Rscript -e "devtools::document()"

However, the pre-commit configuration for safedata includes a step that automatically runs this update. If you try to commit code without updating the matching man files, then the commit will fail and the documentation will have been updated.

Vignettes

R packages contain vignettes that provide additional documentation such as background and how to guides. The source content for vignettes are Rmarkdown files in the vignettes directory and are set up to use the knitr package to convert the Markdown and code to HTML. The following tool can be used to rebuild the vignettes:

 Rscript -e "devtools::build_articles()"

However, the R CMD BUILD process, which is used to generate the source R package for release also builds the vignettes. This is run during both local package checking and on GitHub Action checking.

Website

In addition to using roxygen2 and knitr to maintain the package documentation and vignettes, safedata also uses pkgdown to create a documentation website. This basically builds a complete website and index around the man files as an API reference and the vignettes as explanatory content (‘articles’).

The configuration for this is in the _pkgdown.yml file. This file typically only needs updating when new functions are added, as they need to be added into the reference structure. The website will contain an HTML version of the Rd files and vignettes but also extra content: for example README.md is used to create index.html and other markdown files can be used to provide other content.

You can use the following commands to remove previous website builds and then recreate the website in the docs directory.

Rscript -e " pkgdown::clean_site()"
Rscript -e " pkgdown::build_site()"

The docs directory is not part of the continuous integration of the package as it can be generated automatically from the Rd and Rmd files. The safedata package therefore includes docs in the .gitignore file: you can view the local copy of the website that these commands generate but it is not managed by git.

The actual safedata website can be rebuilt using the pkgdown::deploy_to_branch() command. This automatically builds the website files (as in the local commands above) and commits them to the gh-pages branch in the repository, which is then deployed to the Github Pages URL for the safedata package:

<https://imperialcollegelondon.github.io/safedata/>

Documentation script

For local use, the package and website build steps have been bundled together in build_scripts/build_docs.sh.

Code formatting and linting

The safedata package uses automatic code formatting and linting to maintain consistent code quality and layout.

  • The air formatter provides fast R code formatting, ensuring that changes to the package code follow consistent and stable layout.
  • The jarl linter provides code linting: it inspects the code using a set of rules and warns about programming errors, bugs and suspicious code patterns.

You do not need to install either of these packages manually, as they are included in the pre-commit setup and so are run automatically on any new code. However, if you want to run them independently of pre-commit then you need to install them.

The pre-commit setup

pre-commit is a Python program that automates running a set of quality assurance and maintenance checks whenever git commit is run. If the checks fail, the commit will be aborted and you will need to fix the issues and re-commit your changes. You will need to:

  1. Install pre-commit
  2. Install the pre-commit configuration for the package from within your clone of the safedata repository by using: pre-commit install

The set of checks (‘hooks’) are defined in the .pre-commit-config.yaml configuration file and the current checks are

  • Running roxygen to check if Rd files are up to date.
  • Inspecting the R code to check it can be loaded, contains no browser() or debug() commands, and that the DESCRIPTION file is complete.
  • Code formatting and linting using air and jarl
  • Checks for common file issues: sorting, missing line endings, oversized files and the inclusion of ‘artifact’ files such as .Rhistory files.

Note that some of these steps may make changes to your files to fix issues, such as to update man files and apply formatting. When this happens, the pre-commit step will fail but you can simply add the changed files to the commit and re-commit to add the automatic fixes.

Web mocking

The safedata package uses the internet extensively for downloading package data and metadata. This includes code used in function examples, vignettes and in running tests. The private function safedata:::mock_api() is used in all of these situations to turn off connections to the actual internet and instead serve up content from the inst/api_data folder. This ensures that testing and documentation building is not reliant on internet connections.

If you add new code to the project that requests content from the internet, you will need to extend the set of mocked URLS in the mock_api_urls list in R/api_mockr.R and include links to the expected content from those links.

At some point, this needs to be made optional, to allow a package build to also be tested against live content.

Package test suite

The package contains a test suite used for testing that functions behave as expected. Currently, this largely checks that network failures are handled gracefully. Those have to be passing before the package can be released. The tests are automatically run by R CMD CHECK during Github Actions but can also be run locally using:

Rscript -e "devtools::test()"

If you want to run a single file of tests, use:

Rscript -e "testthat::test_file('tests/testthat/test-local_sdd.R')"

Release cycle

These are the steps needed to release a new version of safedata. GitHub Actions should ensure that main is always building correctly but checking should be repeated during the release process to ensure that everything is up to date.

Configure git

It is easier if git is configured to push new tags along with commits. This essentially just means that new releases can be sent with a single commit, which is simpler and saves GitHub Actions from building both the the code commit and then the tagged version. This only needs to be set once.

set git config --global push.followTags true

Update main ready for a release

Once you have decided that the changes added to main require a new release then you also need to create a PR to update the following files:

  • Update the DESCRIPTION file to increment the version number to the new release. For example, a bug patch release would update the line Version: 1.0.5-9000 to Version: 1.0.6

  • Update NEWS to document the changes since the previous version

When this PR is merged into main, the GitHub Actions will run the testing described above.

Run package build and validation

The GitHub Actions run day-to-day quality checks on the code but a more stringent set of testing is needed to add a package onto CRAN. The set of checks has been compiled into a single script in build_scripts/build_and_check.sh. The content of this script is shown below - you may prefer to run the code step by step and the components are described below.

#!/bin/bash
# Script to build and check safedata

# 0) Show R version being used
R --version

printf "\n------------\n\n"

# 1) Move down into the source directory and update the documents 
#    using Roxygen and pkgdown
cd ../
Rscript -e "devtools::document()"
Rscript -e " pkgdown::clean_site()"
Rscript -e " pkgdown::build_site()"


# 2) Move down again into the parent directory and 
#    build the package from the source directory
cd ../
R CMD BUILD safedata

# 3) Identify the version name that just got built and check it for CRAN
VERSION=$(sed -n -e '4p' safedata/DESCRIPTION  | cut -d " "  -f 2)
R CMD CHECK --as-cran --run-donttest safedata_$VERSION.tar.gz

Two points to note:

  1. The built package and check output are saved in the parent directory of the repository, not in the repository itself.
  2. The version built is the one in the currently checked out branch!

The key file to look at is safedata.Rcheck/00check.log. This contains a long list of checks applied to the code. Look out for NOTE, WARNING and ERROR and resolve these issues before moving on. If you are checking in the develop branch then you will see a note saying Version contains large components - that is about to be fixed.

Checking on different platforms

The GitHub Action build process should now be underway for the main branch. Git Actions is configured (see .github/workflows/check-standard.yaml) to build the package under R stable on Ubuntu, Mac and Windows and R devel on Ubuntu.

Although Windows is included in the GitHub Actions testing environment, the R Project also maintains a Windows test environment that can be used. This needs a built copy of the main branch, so run build_scripts/build_and_check.sh again. This should create a newly built package with the new version number (e.g. safedata_1.0.6.tar.gz). If everything checked out ok before creating the release, this is really just updating the version name.

You then need to upload that file to win-builder. The python script build_scripts/upload_to_win-builder.py will do this for you - it is simply automating the process of using FTP to upload the current version for checking under both R stable and R devel. Note that win-builder communicates by email with the package maintainer (whoever has the cre flag in the authors section of the DESCRIPTION file).

python build_scripts/upload_to_win-builder.py

Wait

Ideally what happens now is that the build and check process on GitHub Actions and win-builder all pass. You must wait for these checks to complete!

Obviously, if any errors or warnings crop up in the checking process, those should be fixed in the release branch. The changes should be committed and pushed to start a new round of GitHub Actions checking and you will need to rebuild and resubmit to win-builder

Final edits

Before submitting the code to CRAN you should make the following changes:

  • Update cran-comments.md to record the R versions and environments used for testing and the outcomes of those builds. This should all be status: OK but there might be notes that should be explained.

You now should also build the final version of the release code to be submitted to CRAN:

cd build_scripts
./build_and_check.sh

That should create the source package in the parent directory (e.g. safedata-1.0.6.tar.gz).

These edits and building will obviously also need to be committed and so there is likely to be one last round of CI runs, but this will just be documentation and information changes and so is unlikely to reveal new issues. Of course, if it does, you’ll have to fix them!

Finish the release

Once the main branch is passing checks on all platforms, then the candidate release is ready to be released as a version. Create a release on the Github release page to tag the specific commit to the main branch that was just used to build the final package version.

Release to CRAN

You can then submit the built version of the source package that was created during the release process at: ()[https://cran.r-project.org/submit.html]

You should take the up-to-date contents of cran-comments.md and copy that in the comments section of the submission form. The CRAN maintainers expect submitted packages to be functional and fully checked and these notes will help them see that the package has been properly checked.
